newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Meister - dollar's level "not appropriate".
newsitem.headline: Buba's Meister - dollar's level "not appropriate".

text.p: Bundesbank directorate member Edgar Meister said on Tuesday that the current dollar exchange rate of below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate".
"The current dollar exchange rate is not appropriate," Meister said at a seminar when asked if the current dollar exchange rate was fitting to the fundamental economic position.

He went on to say that current interest rates were appropriate. "The Bundesbank will continue to follow its current course. Interest rate levels are appropriate. There is no need for the Bundesbank to intervene," said Meister.
Speaking at a conference organised by an association of savings banks in the Rhineland-Palatinate region, Meister said exchange rate levels were no reason to prompt interest rate changes.
Meister said Germany must strive to meet the EMU starting deadline in 1999 and that the chances of that happening were good.
"We have to make the effort to meet the January 1 1999 starting deadline for European currency union," said Meister.
He reasserted the Bundesbank's belief that currency union also had to be a stable union.
